newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Primakov urges broader push on Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Primakov urges broader push on Mideast peace.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov urged parties to the Middle East peace process on Friday to end the Arab-Israeli stalemate and honour agreements already made by their predecessors.
It was time to break out of "a very dangerous and even deadlocked situation" in the region by taking a wider approach, he told a business conference in Switzerland.
"We need to work along all the tracks of settlement without focusing only on the Palestinian-Israeli settlement," he said.

"We need to advance along the Syrian track, the Libyan track, because moving ahead on just one track -- with the slow movement or artificial blocking of movement on another track -- might lead to counterproductive results."
Primakov also called for continuity in the peace process by having new governments adhere to agreements they inherit from previous administrations.

"Every new leadership which comes to power in a given country is obligated to rely on those agreement which have been reached by their predecessors on the way toward peaceful settlement of conflict," he said.
He did not refer specifically to any country by name, but was apparently referring to Israel.
Russia's role as co-sponsor with the United States of Middle East peace talks launched in Madrid has been eclipsed of late by Washington's more high-profile efforts.
A spokesman for President Boris Yeltin said last month Moscow planned new initiatives in the peace process.
Yeltsin has met Israeli Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in recent months, but with no apparent effect on the peace process.
